segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After this there was a festival of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now there is in Jerusalem, by the Sheep Gate, a pool called in Hebrew Bethesda, which has five colonnades.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In these lay a crowd of the sick—blind, lame, paralyzed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One man was there who had been ill for thirty-eight years.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Jesus saw him lying there and learned that he had already been in that condition a long time, he said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do you want to become well?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The sick man answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up; and while I am on my way, someone else goes down ahead of me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Get up, pick up your mat, and walk.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And at once the man became well, and he picked up his mat and began to walk. Now that day was a Sabbath.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Jewish leaders said to the man who had been healed,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “It is the Sabbath, and you are not permitted to carry your mat.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he answered them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “The man who made me well—he told me, ‘Pick up your mat and walk.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They asked him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Who is the man who told you, ‘Pick it up and walk’?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the man who had been cured did not know who it was, for Jesus had slipped away, as there was a crowd in the place.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Afterward Jesus found him in the temple and said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “See, you have become well. Sin no longer, so that nothing worse happens to you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The man went away and told the Jewish leaders that it was Jesus who had made him well.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And for this reason the Jewish leaders began to persecute Jesus, because he was doing these things on the Sabbath.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “My Father is working even until now, and I too am working.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For this reason, then, the Jewish leaders sought all the more to kill him, because he was not only breaking the Sabbath but was also calling God his own Father, making himself equal to God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus answered and said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly, truly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing on his own, only what he sees the Father doing; for whatever the Father does, the Son also does in the same way.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For the Father loves the Son and shows him everything that he himself is doing, and he will show him greater works than these, so that you will be amazed.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to those he wishes.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Nor does the Father judge anyone; he has given all judgment to the Son,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever hears my word and believes the one who sent me has eternal life and does not come into judgment, but has crossed over from death to life.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, an hour is coming, and is now here, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For just as the Father has life in himself, so also he has granted the Son to have life in himself;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and he has given him authority to carry out judgment, because he is the Son of Man.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Do not be amazed at this, for an hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs will hear his voice

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and will come out—those who have done good, to a resurrection of life, and those who have practiced evil, to a resurrection of judgment.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I can do nothing on my own. As I hear, I judge, and my judgment is just, because I do not seek my own will but the will of the one who sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If I testify about myself, my testimony is not true.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: There is another who testifies about me, and I know that the testimony he gives about me is true.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I, however, do not accept testimony from a human being; but I say these things so that you may be saved.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: He was the lamp, burning and shining, and you were willing for a while to rejoice in his light.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But I have a testimony greater than John’s: the works that the Father has given me to complete—the very works I am doing—testify about me that the Father has sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And the Father who sent me has himself testified about me. You have never heard his voice or seen his form,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and you do not have his word remaining in you, because you do not believe the one he sent.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You search the Scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that testify about me,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: yet you are unwilling to come to me so that you may have life.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I do not accept glory from people,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: but I know you: you do not have the love of God within you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I have come in my Father’s name, and you do not accept me; if another comes in his own name, you will accept him.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: How can you believe, when you accept glory from one another and do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father. There is one who accuses you: Moses, on whom you have set your hope.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For if you believed Moses, you would believe me, for he wrote about me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my words?”

notes.note: The Greek has only an adjective, “the sheep-related,” with no noun. Most translations supply “gate,” after the Sheep Gate of Nehemiah 3:1 on the north side of the temple area. Some instead read “by the Sheep Pool there is a place called Bethesda,” and the oldest translations took it that way.

The Greek word means “in the language of the Hebrews” and does not distinguish Hebrew from Aramaic, the everyday language of many Jews in Judea at the time. Several of the names John labels this way are Aramaic in form, so some translations render “in Aramaic.”
The manuscripts give the name in several forms, chiefly Bethesda, Bethzatha and Bethsaida. SBLGNT reads Bethesda; some other critical editions prefer Bethzatha. The original form is uncertain.

notes.traditional: blind, halt, withered, waiting for the moving of the water
notes.note: The earliest manuscripts lack the end of verse 3 and all of verse 4, which is why the numbering passes from 3 to 5. Later manuscripts add that the sick were waiting for the water to move, because an angel came down from time to time and stirred the pool, and the first to step in afterward was healed. Most scholars regard this as an early explanation of verse 7 that entered the text from the margin.

The Greek says simply “the Jews,” as in verse 1. Here and through verse 18 the group in view is the authorities in Jerusalem who police Sabbath observance, not the Jewish people as a whole; Jesus, the healed man and the crowd are all Jews. Scholars are divided on how to render John’s usage, some preferring “Judeans” throughout and others keeping “the Jews” everywhere.

notes.phrase: you are not permitted to carry your mat
notes.note: Carrying a load on the Sabbath was understood to be forbidden work (compare Jeremiah 17:21–22), and later rabbinic law lists carrying an object from one place to another among the prohibited kinds of labor. The objection is to the carrying, not to the healing as such, though verse 16 extends the charge to Jesus.

notes.phrase: My Father is working even until now
notes.note: Genesis says God rested on the seventh day, but Jewish interpreters of the period commonly held that God never stops sustaining the world, giving life and judging, even on the Sabbath. Jesus claims the same exemption for himself, which is why verse 18 treats the saying as a claim to equality with God.
The adjective is formed from the word for “age.” In Jewish usage “eternal life” is the life of the age to come, a matter of kind as well as length. John stresses that the believer has it already.

Only here in the Gospels does the phrase lack the Greek definite articles, so it could mean “a son of man,” that is, a human being: authority to judge is given him because he is human. Most interpreters take it as the title, noting that the Greek of Daniel 7:13, where “one like a son of man” receives authority, also lacks the article.

The language is that of a courtroom. Under the Law a matter had to be established by two or three witnesses (Deuteronomy 19:15), and a person’s unsupported testimony on his own behalf did not count. “Not true” here means not admissible as valid evidence, not that it is false; Jesus goes on to name his other witnesses.

The Greek verb form can be either a statement (“You search”) or a command (“Search”). Older translations took it as a command. Most modern translations and commentators read a statement, since the following words explain why the hearers already do this and the point is that they miss what the Scriptures say.

The phrase can mean love for God or the love that comes from God. Most interpreters take it here as love for God, which the hearers lack despite their devotion to the Scriptures. The translation keeps the ambiguity of the Greek.

candidates.reason: Translations vary between “judgment” and “condemnation” (as at 5:24 and 5:29), and John’s argument depends on the same word recurring.
The verb and its noun μαρτυρία form a central courtroom theme in John and Revelation, and translations vary between “testify/testimony” and “bear witness/witness.”
A key Johannine word rendered variously as “abide,” “remain,” “stay” and “dwell”; the reader should be able to track it across John and 1 John.
Translations vary between “glory,” “honor” and “praise” where human approval is meant, obscuring John’s contrast between glory from people and glory from God.
Recurs in John and Revelation and translations divide between “in Hebrew” and “in Aramaic”; one decision is needed.
